$comment: Loomfall worldgen structure registry. Categories: ruin (the Weaver's abandoned edits), understitch_ghost_terrain (older world-versions showing through), village_camp (settlements and camps of the woven folk), cinderloom_fortress, cinderloom_arena (unique), nevermend_gauntlet (the fixed four-outpost approach set of the final arena), nevermend_arena (unique). Block palettes reference canonical ids from naming.json only. Footprints are {x,y,z} in blocks; y is height. Where an entry carries a variants array, the footprint applies to each variant individually and the set's multiplicity is fixed by its unique_set spawn rule; variant ids are addressable by scoped triggers (see boss.json gauntlet).

structures.name: The Unpicked Manor
structures.spawnRules: biome:bleachlands OR biome:unfinished_hem; terrain:flat, surface_slope<=2; min_spacing:768; must_not_overlap:village_camp
structures.loreHook: The Weaver wove houses too, and liked this one less.
structures.description: A grand threadstone hall stopped mid-course: walls that rise to different heights and simply end, doorways framed onto open air, a staircase that climbs three steps and forgets the rest. Inside, the outlines of furniture are pressed into the loamweft floor where things were unpicked rather than moved. Loomglass panes hang in half the windows; the other half were never drawn. One sealed cellar room holds a loot cache (giltspool, a bindwax nub, a Wickerkin lore-scroll) behind a wall the Weaver did finish. Silence-Moths gather here at night; Needlejacks stand in the empty doorframes and wait for it.

structures.name: The Tangle Spire
structures.loreHook: Some drafts the Weaver did not unpick — only turned away from.
structures.description: A tower of braided thrumwood boles twisted like a rope, abandoned mid-twist: the upper third splays open into loose hanging strands that creak in wind, each thick as a tree. The interior spiral stair is intact to the break. Dead knotlights line the landings — burned past relighting, their captured thread long spent; they can only be harvested. A Needlejack nest occupies the splayed crown (spawner; disable by breaking the nest's raw_skein core), guarding a chest of needle_iron scrap and Dawnthread offcuts. The Thrum is measurably louder inside the braid.

structures.name: The Fallen Loomgate
structures.loreHook: Someone tried to leave the way they came. The fray does not thread twice.
structures.description: A shattered Cinderglass loom-gate frame lying across a half-unravelled island, its black arch snapped in three, the living fray it once held long since gone slack and dark. Threadstone anchor-footings from another realm still cling to its base — the whole gate was torn out of somewhere and drifted here entire. Scattered around it: a ring of voidknot blocks placed by hand, a hemstone slab carved with tally marks, and a cache holding cinderglass, a knotlight, and one skein of scorched_silk. The Unpicked circle this ruin but will not cross the voidknot ring.

structures.name: The Twice-Ford
structures.loreHook: The river remembers running here. On some nights, so does the bridge.
structures.description: A low threadstone footbridge arching over a riverbed that holds no river — the water moved when the Weaver re-drew the valley, but the crossing was never unpicked. The dry channel beneath is floored in understitch_loam (harvestable; the best farm soil in the Downs), and pale loomglass shimmer-blocks hang where the old waterline stood, showing the ghost of the current if you look along them at dusk. Wild spoolmares graze the ghost-banks and are calmest here (raised tame chance within the footprint). No loot chest; the structure IS the loot.

structures.name: The Meadow Beneath the Meadow
structures.spawnRules: biome:sennmeadows OR biome:muslin_fens; terrain:flat, cloth_thinness>=0.4; min_spacing:512
structures.loreHook: Before the meadow, there was a meadow. It has not finished leaving.
structures.description: A circular patch where the present grass wears thin and an older draft shows through: the warpsod here is doubled, and breaking the top layer reveals understitch_loam threaded with an earlier, stranger embroidery pattern. Stumps of thrumwood boles from a forest that no longer exists rise waist-high in a loose ring, and tufts of raw_skein snag on them from skeinlings that come here to graze and stand very still. Standing at the center at night triggers hear_thrum reliably. Occasionally one of The Understruck surfaces here, mourning; it will not attack unless approached.

structures.name: The Unhemmed Stair
structures.loreHook: The way down was drawn before the ground was.
structures.description: A grand threadstone staircase from an earlier draft of the world, descending through ground that was never fully woven — long stretches of the surrounding terrain render as loomglass-clear sketch, so the stair hangs visibly in the world's cross-section. The lowest eleven steps are voidknot, the first a player is likely to see, cold underfoot and utterly solid. The stair ends at a sealed landing containing a cache (hemstone, bindwax, a dead knotlight) and a wall where a fray sometimes opens (structure may host a natural way down to Nevermend; sealing it counts toward the seal_fray trigger once live — note it would fire ahead of its Nevermend-tree parent down_the_fray, so the achievements owner should either accept the out-of-order grant or gate this fray until the player has first entered Nevermend). Frayed Hounds den beneath the mid-flight.

structures.name: Wickerkin Weft-Hamlet
structures.spawnRules: biome:sennmeadows OR biome:thrumwood(edge); terrain:flat, near_water<=48; min_spacing:640; must_not_overlap:ruin
structures.loreHook: They dream they are alive, and they have made the dream hospitable.
structures.description: Five to nine round cottages of knotwood plank on thrumwood-bole frames, roofed in raw skein, windows of wavering loomglass, every lintel hung with knot-charms. A central green holds the hamlet's shared knotlight (usable as anchor), a trading porch (4-6 Wickerkin traders: skeins, dye, knotwork, lore-scrolls; drives trade_with:wickerkin and trade_count), understitch_loam garden plots, and a skeinling pen. The Wickerkin bar their doors at dusk and sing, courteously, until the Needlejacks lose interest. No hostile spawns inside the lit radius. Loot is honest: buy it.

structures.name: The Herders' Picket
structures.loreHook: The Wickerkin do not ride. They keep the mares anyway, for the company.
structures.description: A seasonal Wickerkin herding camp: a picket ring of thrumwood-bole posts strung with cord, three raw-skein tents on plank platforms, a watch-perch, and one knotlight kept burning against the dark. Two or three Wickerkin herders trade thread-sinew, hide-cloth, and spoolmare tack; a small corral holds 2-4 already-gentled spoolmares (greatly raised tame chance — the intended early path to tame_entity:spoolmare). A feed crate holds raw_skein and a saddle-frame of needle_iron. At night the herders drum softly on the picket posts; the mares stand with their heads together like a conversation.

structures.name: The Vigil Waystation
structures.spawnRules: biome:warpspine_reach OR biome:the_frostlace; terrain:mountain_pass OR ridge_saddle; altitude>=surface+40; min_spacing:896
structures.loreHook: You are not the first thread to wake. Others left the light on.
structures.description: A one-room threadstone shelter built into a pass, clearly the work of earlier Menders rather than the Weaver: the stonework is patched, argued-with, mended. Inside: a knotlight on a plinth (free anchor — the whole point of the structure), a mothdust_brick lamp that never flickers, a bunk, and a shared cache the worldgen stocks modestly (threadstone tools, woven_cloth, emberskein_ore for the brazier) with a chance of a dawnthread sliver. Frostlace filigree seals the windows against the cold. A guest-log slate on the wall bears scratch-marks in different hands. Convention says take one thing, leave one thing.

structures.name: The Stitched Stead
structures.loreHook: Someone made it this far, and bound what they could before the rest of them went.
structures.description: A dead Mender's camp in the deep: a causeway of voidknot laid stitch by stitch across the Loosened Dark — you can read the builder's growing exhaustion in the spacing — ending at a tiny hemstone shelter on a fraying island. The shelter's doorframe and cache-chest are worked in bindwax (permanently bound: the Ravelling has stripped the island around them and not touched these). Inside: a knotlight gone cold but not dead — its captured thread still whole — that CAN be relit (rare safe anchor in Nevermend), everthread tempering notes on a hemstone slate, and a cache of hemstone, voidknot, and one bound giltspool charm. Three memorial slates stand outside. There is no body. There is never a body, here.

structures.name: The Scaldwatch Bastion
structures.loreHook: They still stand the watch. No one has told them the watch ended.
structures.description: A four-towered tallowstone bastion straddling a river of molten skein, its cinderglass ramparts black against the forge-light, needle_iron portcullis grates raised and lowered on schedules no one remembers setting. Scaldwarden patrols (6-10, neutral until theft) walk the walls in rotation, pausing at empty niches to report to a Weaver who is not there. Stores: emberskein_ore stockpiles, quenching troughs, scorched_silk bales from tithed Emberspinners. The vault at the bridge's heart holds bindwax and giltspool behind a cinderglass door — taking any of it turns the garrison hostile. Emberspinners web the under-bridge; Waxlings pool in the guardroom hearths.

structures.name: The Spindlegate
structures.loreHook: The gate was built to keep the fire in — not to keep you out. It has forgotten the difference.
structures.description: A colossal gatehouse sealing the canyon that descends to the deepest spindle and Molthkin, the First Bobbin. Twin cinderglass pylons flank a still-turning ember-spindle the size of a keep; its trailing thread bridges the gap and is the only way across (walkable; frays your cloth slowly — bring mending). Scaldwarden wardens of higher rank hold three ascending gates, each with a needle_iron mechanism that must be threaded, not smashed. Garrison spawner in the pylon roots (falls quiet for a while after Molthkin is felled, as the forges briefly still). Loot escalates by gate: emberskein_ore, then quenched scorched_silk, then — behind the last gate — a single strand of everthread laid on a tallowstone altar, an offering awaiting a Weaver who will not collect it. Every Spindlegate canyon descends into the same deep forge-run, and every deep forge-run ends at the Deepest Spindle (id deepest_spindle).

structures.name: The Deepest Spindle
structures.spawnRules: unique:exactly_one_per_world; biome:cinderspindle_forges; terrain:canyon_floor_below_spindlegate_descent; reached_via:spindlegate (per spindlegate spawnRules: gates_descent_to_deepest_spindle — every Spindlegate canyon descends into the same deep forge-run, and every deep forge-run ends here)
structures.loreHook: It has been turning down here since before there was anyone to hear it. It is still waiting. Please do not tell it.
structures.description: The floor of the world's forge: a circular working of scored tallowstone some seventy blocks across, ringed by cinderglass canyon walls lit from behind by the deep fire, with Molthkin, the First Bobbin, turning at its center (boss wiring: molthkin.json). Concentric winding-grooves spiral the floor in to the spindle-shaft; twelve shallow cold-seams are cut among them, sized to take a placed frostlace or mothdust_brick flush with the floor (winding-pull immunity, per bestiary). No slagmoth spawns natively in the biome, but forge vents pierce the walls and deliver them to anything cold left standing, on the arena-local cadence molthkin.json specifies (1 per 20 seconds per standing cold block, cap 4); waxlings shed down the same vents in the fight's second movement. Cooled slag bollards of cinderglass ring the mid-floor: cover, and handholds against the winding. No chests, no garrison, and no loot but the one coil at the heart of the boss. When Molthkin is felled the vents sigh shut and the arena goes dark and still for three day-cycles with the rest of the forges.

structures.name: The Tallow Reliquary
structures.loreHook: In the only cool shadows of the burning realm, they keep what the fire must never finish.
structures.description: A fortified keep carved directly from a tallowstone cathedral wall, lit throughout by cold mothdust_brick — the single structure in the Cinderloom with no open flame, because what it guards must not melt. Behind three cinderglass doors, the reliquary proper: shelves of bindwax blocks and bound giltspool relics, first-draft knotwork the Scaldwardens saved from the fire on their own initiative, the closest thing they have to disobedience. A small Scaldwarden order (4-6) keeps it; they are gentler here, and one will trade quenching-lore for emberskein_ore. Waxlings swarm the entry galleries, drawn to the cool (swarm spawner in the drip-gutters; slick tallow floors). Slagmoths press at the cinderglass doors in burning drifts, drawn to the cool within; keeping them out is the wardens' oldest standing duty, and the cold mothdust light gives them nothing to love. The loot is real — bindwax in quantity found nowhere else — and stealing it is the cruelest theft in the game. The wardens will fight for it, and mourn while they do.

structures.name: The Selvage Outposts
structures.spawnRules: unique_set:exactly_four_per_world; biome:last_selvage; terrain:approach_causeway_of:eye_of_the_last_hem; generated_with:eye_of_the_last_hem (only with, and only once with, the unique arena — the set never places independently of it); placement:evenly_spaced_along_causeway, ordered_per:variants; must_not_overlap:eye_of_the_last_hem
structures.loreHook: A hem is finished in four motions: measure, fold, pin, sew. So, it turns out, is an argument.
structures.description: The four fixed outposts of the Approach Causeway, generated as a set with — only with, and only once with — the Eye of the Last Hem, standing evenly along the single finished-hem way in: The Measured Post, The Folded Post, The Pinned Post, The Sewn Post, named landward to arena mouth for the four motions that finish a hem, and each barrier-chord at the arena mouth takes its outpost's name. Each outpost is a squat hemstone drum raised around an everthread capstan on which one of the four barrier-chords is wound taut, and each seal is held by exactly one spawn-tagged, structure-bound Selvage Warden seal-holder (per bestiary.json: hp 90, damage 9, regenerating 2 hp per second with regeneration suppressed for 3 seconds only by a single hit dealing 6 or more — Dawnthread-tier weapons or better are effectively required) that walks its footprint in slow, exact circuits and never pursues beyond it. The seal is bound to the holder, not to the ground: felling that outpost's seal-holder fires kill_entity:selvage_warden exactly as any warden kill does (achievement argue_past_certainty on the first, exactly as for any first warden) and releases that outpost's seal wherever the body comes to rest — knockback cannot carry the kill out of counting, and a rim-patrol warden that wanders or spawns inside the footprint and dies there releases nothing. The capstan turns once and the chord at the arena mouth goes slack, permanently: released seals never re-knot — not if the Mender is unpicked, not if the arena encounter resets — and a felled seal-holder does not respawn. An unfelled seal-holder restores to full hp when no Mender has stood within the outpost footprint for 10 consecutive seconds, and instantly on the engaged Mender's unpicking; bolts loosed from beyond the threshold buy nothing the mending does not take back. Seal ids and release logic: boss.json gauntlet.seals (all four required, any order). Mothdust_brick way-lamps mark each threshold, and a single prepared voidknot stitch-point beside each capstan accepts a knotlight — an ordinary Nevermend anchor (a Mender unpicked on the causeway re-stitches at the nearest knotted outpost) that does not and cannot satisfy the arena's set_anchor condition, left by Menders who walked the causeway before you and did not all walk the length of it. No cache and no loot tables: the warden's hemstone, the slackened chord, and the way forward are the whole of the yield. The four lowered chords do not fall — they draw inward and coil at the arena's central binding-anvil, waiting to be the thread of the final stitch (boss.json phase 3, The Binding; books.json letter_three_stitches speaks from the far side of them).

structures.name: The Eye of the Last Hem
structures.spawnRules: unique:exactly_one_per_world; biome:last_selvage; terrain:outermost_rim_of_finished_hem; anchored_to_selvage_edge; unlocked_by:approach_with_everthread_gear OR ride_spoolmare_in:nevermend
structures.loreHook: Every hem ends in an eye. Every eye waits for its needle.
structures.description: The throne-country of The Last Needle and the game's final arena: a vast ring of shining hemstone at the absolute rim of reality, woven like the eye of a needle laid flat, with the Loosened Dark below and nothing at all beyond the outer edge. The fighting floor is finished hem — it cannot be broken or built upon except at prepared voidknot stitch-points ringing the arena, where a Mender can lay emergency footing when the Needle unpicks the floor's inner bands (arena hazard: concentric floor sections unravel and re-knit on a cycle). Four Selvage Warden outposts stand the approach causeway (mini-boss gauntlet — structure id selvage_outpost, a fixed set of four generated with this arena; each outpost's seal-holder felled releases its seal, per boss.json gauntlet.seals, and lowers one strand of the everthread barrier-chords at the arena mouth). Mothdust_brick beacon-pyres mark the cardinal points and can be lit to brief safe zones. The pyres and stitch-points are not the Needle's work, nor the Weaver's — Menders came this far before you, and left what they could. At the center, a single everthread stitch-point: the binding-anvil where, at the end, the Needle is not killed but bound, turned, and taught — for a while — to mend (kill_entity:last_needle resolves here). No loot tables. What you leave with is the ending you choose.
